liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Saint Of Circumstance** (2 reviews): Second time played; Weir ad-libs odd lyrics, sounding like a lounge cover band; Described as loose, disco-flavored and far out; an early, rough Weir effort [13][16]
- **Big River** (1 review): Singled out as a standout version [11]
- **Friend Of The Devil** (1 review): Band plays with great intensity on this one [13]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): Listener's first Scarlet>Fire; Jerry misses some lyrics but his guitar work compensates [10]

## The recordings

- **gd1979-09-01.sbd.123742.miller.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 18 songs; 156 min; rated 4.38/5 by 8 [1]
- **gd79-09-01.sbd.dodd.18898.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 18 songs; 158 min; rated 4/5 by 24 [2]. Said about its sound: Sound on the recording is fine [16]
- **gd1979-09-01.145174.fob.nak700.wagner.miller.sirmick.flac1644**: source not stated; 18 songs; 156 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [3]. Said about its sound: All tracks pitch corrected; the tape flip in Drums was patched with a soundboard source [3]
- **gd79-09-01.aud.10363.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 18 songs; 140 min; rated 4.16/5 by 19 [9]. Said about its sound: Audience recording sounds exceptionally good, putting band and crowd in your living room; mastering praised [17]

## Around the show

- Clouds drifting in from the lake kept the daytime outdoor crowd from overheating [10]
- Local curfew at sundown, plus two opening acts (Greg Khin and The Good Rats), shortened the Dead's set [11]
- Hot September day; crowd arrived early, was wild, and one man was beaten bloody in the audience [12]
- Opening acts included the Good Rats; reviewer disliked them but found the Dead high-energy [12]
- Reviewer trimmed drums to fit Half Step through Bertha onto one 80-minute disc [14]
- Cloudy weather and a frantic rush explain the abrupt ending of the show [19]
- Cloudy weather and a frantic rush explain the abrupt ending of the show [20]
- Old concrete stadium with bleacher seats was demolished and is now a business park; once hosted high school football and Rochester Lancers soccer [21]
- Band seems unhurried, in no rush to get anywhere, a relaxed show [10]
- Calls the Half Step/Franklin's and Scarlet/Fire pairings among the best ever [11]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1979-09-01.sbd.123742.miller.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Dolby B) -> Cassette (Dolby C) ->TC2000 EQ (24bit) -> Sonic Solutions -> CD [1]. Also: Sourced from discs supplied by David Gans, with pitch correction help from Joe B. Jones [1]
- **gd79-09-01.sbd.dodd.18898.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [2]
- **gd1979-09-01.145174.fob.nak700.wagner.miller.sirmick.flac1644**: taped by Bob Wagner; transferred by Sirmick and Charlie Miller; source: FOB Nakamichi 700 > Sony D5M Cassette Master (Maxell UDXLII) - taped by Bob Wagner [3]. Also: David Gans and Charlie Miller supplied the patch source for the Drums tape flip [3]
- **gd79-09-01.aud.10363.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording [9]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Holleder Memorial Stadium - September 1, 1979](https://www.dead.net/show/september-1-1979) [23]
- Poster by LiveGRATEFUL.net: [Grateful Dead 1979-09-01 Sat Holleder Memorial Stadium, Rochester, NY](https://www.livegrateful.net/post/1405532051011/grateful-dead-1979-09-01-sat-holleder) [24]
